raw_answer_text:
A1: The switch learns from the source address of every frame it receives, regardless of whether the destination address is found in the table.
A2: It associates the source MAC address with the port on which the frame arrived.
A3: Whether the destination MAC address is found in the switch's address table (and which port it maps to).
A4: The switch floods the frame out all ports except the one it was received on.
A5: Both are flooded out all ports (except the incoming port); broadcast/multicast frames are always flooded, and unknown unicast frames are flooded until learned.
A6: When the destination address maps to the same port the frame arrived on (i.e., source and destination are on the same segment/port).
A7: Once learned, the switch forwards the frame only out the specific port associated with that station instead of flooding it out all ports.
A8: Both ports must be in the forwarding (learning/forwarding) state, not blocking or disabled.
